title: Credits that pay you back
subject: Money

text: A deduction lowers income. A credit lowers the tax itself.
Some credits are refundable: if the credit is bigger than the tax, you can get the difference back.
For workers with low to moderate earned income. Claimed on the return. There is no separate application.
2025 maximums: $649 with no child, $4,328 with one, $7,152 with two, $8,046 with three or more. Investment income must be $11,950 or less.
Up to $2,200 per qualifying child under 17 at the end of 2025. The child needs a work-eligible SSN.
If the credit is more than your tax, the Additional Child Tax Credit can refund up to $1,700 per child. Those refunds are held until mid-February.
What does not count as earned income
Unemployment, Social Security, child support, and interest are not earned income for the EITC.
Wages and self-employment net earnings are. You must have a valid SSN and meet the income limits for your status and number of children.
You had $30,000 in wages and one qualifying child. What is true?

choices.label: You may qualify for the EITC and the Child Tax Credit. Check the limits.
Credits are only for people who itemize.
A credit and a deduction are the same thing.

text: EITC and the Child Tax Credit are the two that move the refund for most working families.
Use the IRS EITC Assistant. Do not trust a preparer who promises a number before seeing your forms.
